admission.justification: Without the persisted-subject and same-run governing-row checks, a syntactically plausible row could hide a changed record or answer no real item while appearing published. The boundary prevents that costly false completion before output is written, while retaining the explicit non-leaf/raise exemptions.

applicability: Ordinary converted-memory leaf Writer runs consuming the persisted leaf worklist before memory-file publication.
conditions: A missing or unreadable consumed worklist shape refuses with the native compute/recompute remedy; wave and crossing owners do not acquire a leaf-worklist prerequisite.
Non-raise still_rejected, planned and hunk rows must name actual worklist subjects; handle resolution and membership aliases use the native subject population.
A record first authored by this leaf needs no unnecessary judgment when no item names it; raise rows remain exempt from these subject checks.

Every matching touched/stale invariant comparison and guarantee-changed family item is tested by the shared governing-row predicates, without allowing an earlier item lacking comparison facts to hide a later violation.
exclusions: This is the Writer boundary, not a claim that arbitrary caller data is cryptographically unforgeable or that this module recomputes the native worklist.
Admission still needs genuine owner-selected persisted inputs; semantic truth, task-question publication and the independent commit/gate checks keep their own owners.
statement: Leaf Writer rows must agree with the genuine persisted worklist and governing changed-row predicates, while waves and crossing owners have no leaf-worklist prerequisite and raise needs no item.
